scores.claim_text: Columbia Class submarine electric power & propulsion as forward backlog anchor.
supports: pentagon_jbook entry for COLUMBIA Class Submarine exists (program_id columbia-class-submarine, pe_number 1045, P-40 procurement line item, Page 51 of SCN_Book.pdf, FY 2027 Navy Shipbuilding) but funding_history is empty in the corpus extraction; signal=NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE.

usaspending search for 'Leonardo DRS Naval Power Systems' returned 0 awards under that exact recipient string (the propulsion subsidiary contracts likely sit under prime Electric Boat / Newport News rather than direct to DRS in the DoD obligations file).
scores.interpretation: Corpus coverage gap, not a red flag. The Columbia program is real and a flagship Navy procurement; the J-Book corpus did not extract funding numbers for this P-40 line. Treat as UNVERIFIABLE per heuristic #7 (NOT_FOUND != red flag when the corpus is known to be incomplete on that line).

scores.claim_text: DRS opened a 140K sq ft naval power facility in SC + $45M for 40K sq ft expansion, predicated on Navy submarine/shipbuilding funding remaining strong.
supports: Columbia Class itself: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE (cannot affirm or deny funding trajectory).

Virginia Class Submarine (PE 2013) primary_match: signal=FUNDED_SHRINKING. P-40 history shows FY2025=$7,356.9M -> FY2026=$2,740.3M (>60% YoY procurement cut). This is the second-largest Navy program where DRS supplies sub-systems and is highly material to the 'next-generation electric fleet' growth narrative.

DRS capex up 60% YoY in 2025 with the SC facility expansion sized for a multi-year ramp; if Navy submarine procurement is compressing on the Virginia line, the marginal capex ramp is exposed to absorption risk.
scores.interpretation: The forward-looking capacity expansion narrative is partially anchored on Navy submarine program continuity. Columbia is not in the J-Book timerange we can verify, but the adjacent Virginia Class line shows a sharp FY26 procurement contraction. MODERATE: capex absorption risk is real if the broader submarine procurement compresses, even though Columbia itself is structurally protected as a sole-source SSBN program.

scores.claim_text: Counter-drone + SHORAD programs cited as 2025 revenue driver.
supports: pentagon_jbook M-SHORAD (PE 8082C14300, Army Missile Procurement P-40): signal=FUNDED_GROWING. FY25 $69.1M -> FY26 $631.1M -> FY27 $712.7M (10x procurement ramp into FY26).

USAspending: DRS Sustainment Systems received $431M Abrams Active Protection System contract (largest single award in 2025), $77M Tank Rack Modules, $34M NRE, $31M Mobile Gun Solution. Real revenue from named Army ground-vehicle programs.
scores.interpretation: The SHORAD pipeline is in a sharp procurement ramp. PASS; the company's forward-looking SHORAD narrative is well-supported by the J-Book funding trajectory.

scores.claim_text: Counter-sUAS Intercept is a 'sustained DoW priority' and a forward demand driver for DRS force protection systems.
supports: pentagon_jbook Counter sUAS Intercept (PE 9216C82200, Army P-40, page 134 Missile_Procurement_Army.pdf): primary_match signal=FUNDED_STEADY but the corpus' status_declared field for this entry is UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS. History: FY25 $329.2M actual; FY26 enacted is null (not yet booked). The discrepancy is that the auto-derived signal called it FUNDED_STEADY because $329M flowed in FY25, but the declared corpus state is that out-year funding is zero.
DRS does not quantify revenue specifically attributed to the C-sUAS Intercept line; this is a forward 'sustained priority' assertion, not booked revenue.
scores.interpretation: Mixed signal: one-year procurement was real (FY25 $329M) but the declared status flags the out-years as unfunded. Heuristic #2 says forward-narrative-load-bearing 'we expect to compete' claims with UNFUNDED status downgrade to MODERATE. Since DRS frames C-UAS as a sustained priority area rather than a booked revenue stream, MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY is appropriate.

scores.claim_text: 80% of 2025 revenue from U.S. government (Navy 36% + Army 36%); funded backlog $4.6B.
supports: usaspending.query_dod_contracts (recipient_name='Leonardo DRS') returned 1,302 DoD awards totaling $1,768M obligated across DRS subsidiary entities (DRS Sustainment Systems, DRS Network & Imaging Systems, DRS Global Enterprise Solutions, DRS Systems). The recipient-name string match underweights the actual total (Leonardo DRS reported 80% of $3,648M = $2,918M from US-gov in 2025), but the DoD-only obligation pool of $1.77B is directionally consistent with Navy+Army=72% of $3.6B revenue (~$2.6B implied).

Top 15 awards span all four DRS subsidiaries: Abrams Active Protection ($431M), DAIRCM ($232M), MFoCS Processing Unit ($89M), M1200 services ($100M), Tank Rack Modules ($77M), Voice Comms ($76M), IBAS spare NSNs ($43M), JETS Target Locator ($37M), 2nd-Gen FLIR Thermal Receiver ($32M).
scores.interpretation: Independent USAspending data fully corroborates the customer-concentration claim and identifies the specific DoD program lines DRS sits on. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Electronic Warfare (EW) is a core forward capability within ASC + integrated into SHORAD ground vehicles.
supports: pentagon_jbook EW search returns 3 Air Force PEs (Electronic Warfare Development 0604270F, Joint Counter RCIED EW 0205671F, Multi-Platform EW Equipment 0207040F). Primary match (Multi-Platform EW Equipment) shows UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS (FY24 $14.3M -> FY25 $0 -> FY26 $0).
However: DRS does ground-vehicle / SHORAD EW (Army domain via RADA acquisition) — Air Force RCIED / Multi-Platform PEs are not the right verifiers. The Army ground-vehicle EW PE is not in the corpus.
Entity-resolution miss: per cohort guidance, the 10-K's EW claim resolves to Army Tactical Land Aerial Integrated Sensors (TLAIS) / RADA radar-cued EW work, not the AF PEs the keyword search returns.
scores.M_value: Multi-Platform EW Equipment UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS (Air Force PE, wrong domain)
scores.interpretation: The keyword match returns Air Force EW PEs, but DRS's EW work is in Army ground-vehicle integration. Per heuristic #7 + entity-resolution guidance, NOT_FOUND-equivalent for the relevant Army EW PE in our corpus. Score UNVERIFIABLE rather than penalizing the company for an entity-resolution miss.

scores.claim_text: Quantum cascade laser license drove 2025 margin expansion (one-time non-recurring).
supports: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for 'Quantum Cascade Laser' — this is a technology license, not a DoD program element, so corpus mismatch is expected (heuristic #7).
scores.interpretation: Self-acknowledged one-time license, not a program-element-level disclosure. UNVERIFIABLE — but worth flagging that ~$X of the 100bps gross-margin expansion is non-recurring and unlikely to repeat in 2026.

scores.claim_text: Legacy ground surveillance program triggered a 2025 program charge (~2% of revenue net negative EAC adj = $59M).
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext returned 0 hits for 'Leonardo DRS legacy ground surveillance' — the company does not name the program, and no third-party counterparty filing discloses it either.
The EAC adjustment magnitude itself is disclosed ($59M 2025 vs $25M 2024 vs $23M 2023 = 2.4x escalation), which is corroborative of underlying program stress within ASC.
scores.interpretation: DRS withheld the program name. UNVERIFIABLE via external sources, but the EAC adjustment trajectory (2.4x YoY growth in net-negative adjustments) is itself a Mode B yellow flag: rising contract-estimate-at-completion charges suggest portfolio-execution risk. Note as soft red flag without escalating severity.

scores.claim_text: DRS operates ~40 manufacturing/engineering sites across 17 US states, Canada, and Israel.
supports: epa_frs.query_facilities found 1 Leonardo DRS facility in MO (Bridgeton, 4201 Innovation Way) — consistent with the 10-K Item 2 disclosure of a Bridgeton MO IMS facility.

scores.interpretation: EPA FRS partial confirmation; full coverage would require searching each subsidiary name (DRS Network & Imaging, DRS Sustainment, RADA USA). PASS — facility footprint claim is consistent with the limited verification we did.

scores.claim_text: Patent portfolio covering EO/IR focal plane arrays, rugged computers, semiconductor devices.
supports: uspto_odp.query_assignee (DRS Network & Imaging Systems): 52 granted patents pre-cutoff, 99 total applications. Recent grants/applications include 'HIGH-DENSITY CAPACITOR FOR FOCAL PLANE ARRAYS', 'METHOD AND SYSTEM FOR FABRICATION AND USE OF A SPECTRAL BASIS FILTER', and 'SYSTEM AND TECHNIQUES FOR TRANSMISSION INTEGRAL GENERATOR/LINE INTERFACE UNIT MAGNETICS INTEGRATION' — directly mapping to claimed FPA + power generation IP.
Search under 'Leonardo DRS' parent name returned 0 — patents are filed by subsidiaries, again an entity-resolution issue.
scores.M_value: 52 granted patents, FPA-related CPC classes confirmed
scores.interpretation: Strong USPTO corroboration of the EO/IR FPA + rugged computing IP claim. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Germanium supply shortage already impacted EO/IR optics & IR programs in 2025; forward execution risk.
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext returned 0 hits for 'germanium infrared focal plane' — no counterparty filings appear to disclose germanium-driven IR program stress at DRS.

However the self-disclosure is specific and corroborated by general industry context (China germanium export controls began 2023-2024); the company has flagged it as an actual P&L impact, not speculative.
scores.interpretation: The germanium IR supply-chain risk is self-disclosed and historically validated, but no external counterparty disclosure is available via edgar_fts. UNVERIFIABLE via available M-sources. This is a structural cost-of-revenues headwind for ASC's IR product line in 2026.

scores.claim_text: Foreign ownership by Leonardo S.p.A. (Italy); operates under DoW Amended & Restated Proxy Agreement dated 2025-03-01.
supports: edgar_fts.query_fulltext returned 0 hits for 'Leonardo DRS proxy agreement Department of Defense' — the 8-K dated March 12, 2025 (Exhibit 10.1) is the primary source but did not surface in the fulltext index under this query string.
The fact pattern (Italian parent, 2025 Proxy Agreement amendment, classified-contract conditionality) is self-disclosed and consistent across multiple 10-K sections.
scores.interpretation: Self-disclosed governance structure; not flagged as deteriorating. UNVERIFIABLE via external counterparty filings but no signal of stress. Worth noting for cohort context: CFIUS / DoD proxy regime is an idiosyncratic deal-block risk distinct from program funding.

headline_findings: Mode B catch: USAspending shows DRS's single largest 2025 contract ($431M) is Abrams Active Protection System (=Trophy APS hardware), MFoCS Processing Unit ($89M), and DAIRCM ($232M) — all named programs the 10-K does NOT disclose by name. The 10-K talks only in capability categories ('force protection', 'network computing', 'IR sensing'), masking which named programs drive the $1.77B DoD obligation pool.

J-Book signal: Virginia Class Submarine procurement is down 63% YoY (FY25 $7.36B -> FY26 $2.74B). DRS's $45M + 140K sf SC naval power facility expansion is sized for sustained Navy submarine ramp; near-term Virginia compression is a yellow flag even though Columbia (DRS's flagship SSBN exposure) is structurally protected.
J-Book signal: M-SHORAD procurement is in a 10x FY25->FY26 ramp ($69M -> $631M -> $713M); SHORAD/C-UAS narrative is well-supported.

J-Book signal: Counter-sUAS Intercept (PE 9216C82200) shows FY25 $329M but FY26 enacted is null; declared corpus status is UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS. C-UAS pipeline is structurally narrower than the 10-K narrative implies.

Soft signal: EAC negative-adjustment magnitude grew 2.4x YoY (FY23 $23M -> FY24 $25M -> FY25 $59M = ~2% of revenue), with one unnamed 'legacy ground surveillance program' as the largest contributor. Rising EAC adjustments are a Mode B leading indicator of portfolio-execution stress.
Quantum cascade laser license is a non-recurring 2025 margin contributor — gross margin compression is likely in 2026 absent another one-time item.

Coverage gaps: J-Book corpus lacks funding history for Columbia Class (P-40 line 1045 indexed but no FY-by-FY data extracted), lacks Army ground-vehicle EW PEs that are the right verifier for DRS's EW claims, and lacks any quantum-cascade-laser / focal-plane-array R&D PEs.
